item.text: The Crime and Corruption Commission examined Queensland local government corruption risks using complaints, investigations, intelligence and public information from July 2020 to June 2025.
item.support:
complaints received by the CCC relating to the local government sector between 1 July 2020 and 
30 June 2025

item.text: It grouped councils by shared characteristics while recognising that location, size, climate and local industry shape individual councils’ risks.
item.support:
corruption 
risks and vulnerabilities are shaped by factors unique to the location, size, climate and primary industry

item.text: The CCC identified management of people, processes and public assets as high-risk activities, and reported that elected officials were overrepresented in complaints.
item.support: Managing people, processes and public assets are consistently high-risk activities for the sector.

item.text: The CCC outlined prevention measures including internal controls, employee screening, training, supervision, information management, audits and support for reporting wrongdoing.
item.support: Some strategies that can help prevent corruption in local government include:

While there are some consistent trends and themes across the local government sector, corruption 
risks and vulnerabilities are shaped by factors unique to the location, size, climate and primary industry 
of each council area.
